questions.q: Which sidebar entry holds the businesses the equipment is ultimately for?
questions.e: Companies are who we sell to. End Customers are who the kit is for, so competing resellers' deals can roll up under one of them.

questions.q: The Next Actions widget sorts open opportunities by next-step date. Where do deals with no date at all appear?
o: At the top, with the overdue ones
questions.e: Overdue and undated deals float to the top. The widget is deliberately sort-based rather than date-filtered so it never goes stale.

questions.q: A contact signs off the budget. What Decision Role do you set?
questions.e: Economic Buyer is whoever controls the money. Champion sells for us internally; Technical Evaluator tests the kit.

questions.q: A prepay account places an order. What is issued?
o: A Pro Forma, paid before anything is dispatched
questions.e: Prepay accounts get a Pro Forma for payment before dispatch. Credit accounts get a Sales Order confirmation and are invoiced on terms after dispatch.

questions.q: The rule of thumb for who owns what?
o: Whoever opened the email owns everything
If it is about winning the money it is sales; if it is about delivering on the promise it is Customer Operations
Sales owns the customer, Ops owns the system
Ops owns everything until the order is placed
questions.e: Sales keeps the relationship, the pricing and every commercial decision. Ops owns the quoting admin, order processing, supplier and courier chasing, and keeping the customer informed. When in doubt it goes through sales@ and gets an owner either way.

questions.q: What does the Kill the Zebra view track?
questions.e: It collects live displacement plays, tagged with the competitor displaced. It is a strategic scoreboard rather than a revenue view.

questions.q: Where does an order live once it is placed?
questions.e: Intact is the system of record for orders, stock and invoicing. The CRM holds the pursuit; quoteRef and accountCode are how the two tie together.

questions.q: What must be true before a deal sits at Proposal?
o: A formal quotation or proposal has been issued
The close date is inside this quarter
questions.e: Proposal means the quote is in the customer's hands. That is also when the Intact quotation number goes into quoteRef and amountBasis flips to QUOTED.

questions.scenario: You meet a reseller on Tuesday. They want pricing on a fleet of rugged handhelds for one of their retail clients, roughly a hundred units, and they need it in for their client's Q1. You have not quoted anything yet.
questions.q: What do you do before the end of the day?
o: Wait until the quote is ready, then create the opportunity at Proposal
Create the opportunity at Screening with an estimated amount, a close date, the end customer linked and a dated next step
Email yourself a reminder and create it at the Monday review
Create it at New with just the company name and fill the rest in later
questions.e: Same day, from the company record. Screening is right - there is a real need, a named contact and a rough size. An estimated amount with amountBasis ESTIMATED, a realistic closeDate, the endCustomer link and one dated next step is a minute's work and makes the deal real.
